title: Anthrobots and Xenobots share similar movement types and transition profiles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anthrobots and Xenobots share similar movement types and transition profiles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Anthrobots and Xenobots both show discrete movement types with very low interconversion between linear and circular motion (0.2% and 0.3% for Anthrobots, 0.5% and 1.6% for Xenobots) and highly consistent circular behaviour (92% and 95%), though Anthrobot linear behaviour is more consistent (80% versus 67%).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The interconversion between linear and circular is very small for Xenobots (0.5% and 1.6%) and Anthrobots (0.2% and 0.3%), while their consistency of Circular behavior is extremely high for Xenobots (95%) just like for Anthrobots (92%).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Discussion”. Scope: Human NHBE-derived Anthrobots compared with Xenopus laevis Xenobots

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The percentages make the comparison precise and computationally straightforward. Existing publications can check reported values, but harmonized data are needed to determine whether similarity exceeds methodological artifacts.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute identically defined transition matrices for Anthrobot and Xenobot trajectories and compare linear-circular conversion and state-persistence estimates with uncertainty.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cross-study recording and preprocessing may differ.

Raw trajectories for both platforms may not be jointly public.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.84
discriminating power: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.5
data existence: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A public Xenobot tracking archive and its analysis code can re-estimate movement-type persistence for the frog constructs, which is half of the numerical comparison. The Anthrobot percentages come from coordinates that were not released. Matching summary rates would still leave index definitions and biological interpretation only partly tested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute, from public Xenobot tracks and from Anthrobot tracks if released, the self-transition rates of circular and linear segments and the cross-transition rates between them. Overlapping very low linear-circular exchange and circular consistency near the reported 92–95% would support the shared profile; Xenobot rates far from 0.5–1.6% and 95%, once the same indices are used, would refute the Xenobot half.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Straightness and gyration as defined for Anthrobots may not match the Xenobot behavior features.

Anthrobot segment labels are not in that repository.

Similar transition percentages do not show that the two platforms share a mechanism.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.4
data existence: 0.42
data adequacy: 0.32
operationalizability: 0.84
